## 1601 N Milwaukee Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN: 14313320180000 | West Town (Community Area 24)**

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B3-2 (Community Shopping, dash-2 density)** per the City's official GIS parcel records (Ordinance No. 17230). Verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Ground-Floor Retail + Apartments Above?

**Yes, this is a permitted by-right combination.** [1] describes B3 as accommodating a broad range of retail and service uses. [2] confirms that dwelling units located above the ground floor are permitted (P) in B3 districts without special approval. Ground-floor residential is more restricted in B3 — dwelling units *below* the second floor require further review per [2]. Verify: [2] (§17-3-0200 use table).

---

### 3. Bulk & Density Standards

All figures are from the zoning table for B3-2 [1], [3]:

| Standard | B3-2 Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 2.2 |
| **Max Height** | 45–50 ft (varies by lot frontage & ground-floor commercial) |
| **Min Lot Area / Dwelling Unit** | 1,000 sq ft |
| **Lot Coverage** | Not specified in retrieved standards |
| **Setbacks** | Not specified in retrieved standards |

**Unit yield:** With 11,951 sq ft of lot area, the arithmetic allows up to **11 dwelling units** (11,951 ÷ 1,000 = 11.95, rounded down). This is a lot-area-per-unit ceiling only — FAR, height, parking, and other standards may reduce this further. Efficiency and SRO units count at smaller per-unit areas and could allow more [3]. Cite: §17-3-0402 [3].

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

This parcel carries a significant stack of overlays:

- **Individual Landmark Building** — This is flagged as an **individually designated Chicago landmark** (the Noel State Bank building, per Cook County records). Exterior alterations and demolition require approval from the Commission on Chicago Landmarks. This is the most binding constraint for any project.
- **Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** — Located within a City-designated historic district. Alterations affecting historic character are subject to landmarks review.
- **Wicker Park Historic District (National Register)** — Listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Federal historic tax credits may be available for qualifying rehabilitation; federal Section 106 review applies to federally funded/licensed projects.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — Within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station (Damen Blue Line, just 0.07 miles away). Triggers transit-served location standards per [4] (§17-3-0308).
- **ADU Eligible Area** — Accessory dwelling units may be permitted under Chicago's ADU ordinance.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any project seeking an entitlement (zoning change, PD, etc.) will trigger ARO affordable housing obligations. The West Town community area has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 affordable units already in the pipeline.
- **Special Service Area — Wicker Park SSA** — Property is subject to SSA 33 levy (reflected in the tax bill at ~$2,363/yr).
- **No Planned Development** — Not currently in a Planned Development.
- **No Lakefront Protection, no PMD, no special district.**

Verify overlays: [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) and the Commission on Chicago Landmarks ([chicago.gov/landmarks](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/landmarks_designationprocess.html)).

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

Because this parcel is within 2,640 feet of the Damen Blue Line CTA station (a transit-served location), **the minimum parking requirement can be reduced by up to 100%** under §17-10-0102-B [4]. In plain terms, a qualifying project here could provide **zero off-street parking** by right, without a variance. This applies as long as the project complies with the transit-served location criteria of [4] (§17-3-0308). No density, FAR, or height bonus applies at B3-2 — those lot-area and density reductions are available only in dash-3 districts [3].

---

### 6. Demolition & New Mixed-Use Construction

**This is where the landmark designation is decisive.** Because this building is an **individually designated Chicago landmark** (Noel State Bank), demolition is almost certainly prohibited or requires a full Commission on Chicago Landmarks review and likely City Council approval — this is not a standard permit process. Exterior alterations, even short of demolition, require landmarks approval.

Beyond the landmark issue, a new mixed-use building on this site would also need to:

- Satisfy B3-2 bulk standards (FAR 2.2, 45–50 ft max height, 1,000 sq ft/unit) [1], [3]
- Comply with transit-served location criteria per [4] (§17-3-0308), including pedestrian street standards (§17-3-0504)
- Meet ARO obligations if any entitlement (zoning map amendment, PD) is sought
- A density bonus (reduced lot area per unit) is **not available by right** at B3-2 — it would require a Type 1 Map Amendment or Planned Development, and only in dash-3 districts [3]
- Demolition/wrecking permits would be required under the Building Code [5]

**Flood & environmental note:** The parcel is in FEMA Zone X (minimal flood hazard) — no flood insurance requirement. One nearby brownfield site (Park 512 Avenue Park, EPA ID 110005863100) warrants environmental due diligence.

---

### Confidence & What Could Not Be Determined

**High confidence:** Zoning classification, bulk standards, overlay designations, parking reduction, landmark flag, and ARO zone — all from authoritative city GIS and Cook County parcel records.

**Could not determine from retrieved data:** Specific setback requirements, lot coverage maximum, and exact ground-floor commercial height minimums (not in the retrieved code text — consult §17-3-0500 series). Assessment history and prior sales are not available for this parcel. The precise scope of the landmark designation (contributing vs. non-contributing, exact protections) should be confirmed directly with the Commission on Chicago Landmarks at (312) 744-3200.

---

*This information is based on official city documents but does not constitute legal advice. Please consult a licensed attorney or contact the Department of Planning and Development and the Commission on Chicago Landmarks for official guidance before proceeding.*
